relevance_reason: A large Chinese CCDD cohort that includes 2 unrelated sporadic CFEOM probands with the TUBB3 E410K variant. Both had syndromic features (absent olfactory bulbs, facial weakness, intellectual impairment, hypogonadism/Kallmann criteria), which adds further cases to this entry.

findings.statement: Jia et al. (2022) described 2 unrelated Chinese Han probands with CFEOM and the TUBB3 E410K variant: an 11-year-old boy (C21) and a 19-year-old woman (C32), neither with a family history. Both had bilateral ptosis, exotropia, limited horizontal and vertical eye movements, corneal exposure, facial weakness, intellectual impairment and impaired gait. On MRI, both had absent or dysplastic olfactory bulbs and sulci, hypoplasia of the oculomotor nerve and extraocular muscles, absent facial nerves, and malformations of the corpus callosum, anterior commissure and lateral ventricles. The boy had cryptorchidism, and infertility was found in the woman at follow-up.
quotes: The two most common variants were R262C (54.5%, 6/11) and E410K (18.2%, 2/11), less commonly, R380C (9.1%, 1/11), R262H (9.1%, 1/11) and a novel variant S78T (9.1%, 1/11).

Patient C32 exhibits hypoplasia of CC (d3), asymmetry of LV (d4), absence of olfactory bulbs and sulci (d5, arrow), hypoplasia of CN3 (d6) and absence of bilateral CN7 (d7, d8, arrow). The MRI was taken at the age of 19y
Facial weakness and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism occurred in the patients harboring E410K and R262H variants. Psychomotor retardation occurred in patients with R380C, E410K and R262H variants.

phenotypes.text: absence of olfactory bulbs and sulci

findings.statement: Jia et al. (2022) reported that 3 patients with the TUBB3 E410K or R262H variant (C21, C32 and C52) met the diagnostic criteria for Kallmann syndrome. The authors suggested that TUBB3 may be involved in the pathogenesis of Kallmann syndrome.
quotes: In present study, three patients with TUBB3 E410K and R262H variants (C21, C32 and C52) fitted the diagnostic criteria of Kallmann syndrome, confirmed the previous report results and suggested that TUBB3 gene may involve in the pathogenesis of Kallmann syndrome.

findings.statement: Jia et al. (2022) found that CFEOM patients with the TUBB3 R380C, E410K or R262H variant all had multiple congenital craniocerebral and systemic malformations, whereas patients with R262C or S78T had milder, mostly isolated CFEOM. Absent facial nerves and dysplasia of the olfactory bulbs and sulci were associated with the R262H and E410K variants. The authors noted that patients with the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome' are easily misdiagnosed as having Mobius syndrome.
quotes: The patients harboring R262C and S78T showed milder phenotypes compared to the patients with R380C, E410K and R262H variants.
Absence of facial nerves (CN7) and dysplasia of olfactory bulbs and sulci (OBS) were correlated with R262H and E410K variants (Figs. 6, 7).

Furthermore, the patients with “TUBB3 E410K syndrome” and “TUBB3 R262H syndrome” were easily misdiagnosed as MBS owing to similar clinical manifestations (facial weakness and limitation of eye movements etc.).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal morphology of the olfactory bulb

findings.statement: Using whole exome sequencing confirmed by Sanger sequencing, Jia et al. (2022) identified the heterozygous TUBB3 c.1228C-T variant (E410K) in 2 of 11 Chinese CFEOM probands carrying TUBB3 variants. Both probands were sporadic cases.
quotes: Five variants (R262C, R262H, E410K, R380C and S78T) were identified in TUBB3 gene in 11 CFEOM families.
B Five heterozygous variants (S78T, R262C, R380C, E410K and R262H) of TUBB3 gene (red arrows)

relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with TUBB3 E410K syndrome (CFEOM3A1) that adds childhood-onset NASH as an associated feature, with liver immunohistochemistry.

findings.statement: Mori et al. (2022) reported an 11-year-old girl who had been followed since infancy as having atypical Mobius syndrome. She was born with bilateral ptosis, paralytic strabismus, and facial weakness. At age 7 years, whole-exome sequencing gave a diagnosis of TUBB3 E410K syndrome.
quotes: An 11-year-old girl has been followed up as having atypical Möbius syndrome since infancy, as she was born with bilateral ptosis, paralytic strabismus, and facial weakness.
At age 7 years, she was diagnosed with TUBB3 E410K syndrome by whole-exome sequencing.

findings.statement: Mori et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to identify the TUBB3 E410K variant in a girl with congenital bilateral ptosis, paralytic strabismus, and facial weakness. She had previously been diagnosed with atypical Mobius syndrome.
quotes: At age 7 years, she was diagnosed with TUBB3 E410K syndrome by whole-exome sequencing.

findings.statement: Mori et al. (2022) reported that a girl with TUBB3 E410K syndrome had elevated liver transaminases from age 10 years that persisted for almost 2 years. Liver biopsy was suggestive of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The authors described this as the first case of TUBB3 E410K syndrome accompanied by NASH.
quotes: At age 10 years, her blood examination revealed elevated liver transaminase levels, which persisted for almost 2 years. She underwent liver biopsy, the results of which were suggestive of NASH.
We report the first case of TUBB3 E410K syndrome accompanied by NASH.

findings.statement: In the patient's liver, Mori et al. (2022) found that TUBB3 was not expressed in the parenchymal nerve fibers, although tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) was. In contrast, an autopsy case of NASH and a normal control both showed coexpression of TUBB3 and TH. The authors suggested that the TUBB3 mutation may be associated with the pathogenesis and progression of NASH.
quotes: The expression of TUBB3 was absent, but that of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) was present in the parenchymal nerve fibers of the liver.
On the other hand, in comparison with an autopsy case of NASH and a normal control, these showed coexpression of TUBB3 and TH in the liver.
This case suggests that the TUBB3 mutation may be associated with the pathogenesis and progression of NASH in humans.

relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with a de novo TUBB3 E410K mutation (the variant behind CFEOM3A syndromic), plus a review of the E410K phenotype.

findings.statement: Dentici et al. (2020) reported a 3-year-old boy whose complex phenotype included severe bilateral palpebral ptosis that did not respond to eye surgery, psychomotor delay, absent speech, hypogonadism, celiac disease, and cyclic vomiting. Brain MRI showed thinning of the corpus callosum and no evidence of malformative cortical dysplasia.
quotes: We report on a 3-year-old boy in whom clinical exome sequencing allowed to identify a de novo TUBB3 E410K mutation as the molecular cause underlying a complex phenotype characterized by a severe bilateral palpebral ptosis refractory to eye surgery, psychomotor delay, absent speech, hypogonadism, celiac disease, and cyclic vomiting.
Brain MRI revealed thinning of the corpus callosum with no evidence of malformation cortical dysplasia.

findings.statement: In a 3-year-old boy with this syndromic phenotype, Dentici et al. (2020) used clinical exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous recurrent mutation in the TUBB3 gene, c.1228G>A (p.E410K).
quotes: A recurrent heterozygous mutation, c.1228G > A; p.E410K, in TUBB3 gene is responsible of a rare disorder clinically characterized by congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscle type 3 (CFEOM3), intellectual disability and a wide range of neurological and endocrine abnormalities.
clinical exome sequencing allowed to identify a de novo TUBB3 E410K mutation as the molecular cause

findings.statement: Dentici et al. (2020) reviewed reported patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation and compared them with patients carrying other TUBB3 mutations. They concluded that E410K causes a clinically recognizable syndrome of CFEOM3, intellectual disability, and neurologic and endocrine abnormalities, and that it is not associated with the distinct cortical dysplasia caused by other mutations in the same gene.
quotes: We reviewed available records of patients with TUBB3 E410K mutation and compared their phenotype with the clinical outcome of patients with other mutations in TUBB3 gene.
The present study confirms that TUBB3 E410K results in a clinically recognizable phenotype, unassociated to the distinct cortical dysplasia caused by other mutations in the same gene.

phenotypes.text: congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles

findings.statement: Dentici et al. (2020) stated that early molecular characterization of TUBB3 E410K syndrome is critical for targeted genetic counseling and for timely neurologic, ophthalmologic, endocrine, and gastrointestinal follow-up.
quotes: Early molecular characterization of TUBB3 E410K syndrome is critical for targeted genetic counseling and prompt prospective care in term of neurological, ophthalmological, endocrine, and gastrointestinal follow-up.

relevance_reason: The paper describes the neuroimaging and neuropsychological phenotype of 7 patients with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome (CFEOM3A1), adding detail on white matter changes.

findings.statement: Grant et al. (2019) studied 7 unrelated individuals (4 children and 3 adults) with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome. All had a de novo heterozygous TUBB3 c.1228G>A (E410K) mutation. They had intellectual and social disabilities but no cortical malformations. Compared with 22 controls on structural and diffusion MRI, the patients had decreased corpus callosum volume and decreased network efficiency. All patients showed an aberrant corticospinal tract trajectory and absence of the long segment of the dorsal language network on both sides.
quotes: Seven unrelated individuals (four pediatric, three adults) with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome, harboring identical de novo heterozygous TUBB3 c.1228 G>A mutations, underwent neuropsychological testing and neuroimaging.
Despite the absence of cortical malformations, they have intellectual and social disabilities.
All subjects showed aberrant corticospinal tract trajectory and bilateral absence of the dorsal language network long segment.

phenotypes.text: bilateral absence of dorsal language network long segment

findings.statement: Grant et al. (2019) found that the imaging changes in TUBB3 E410K syndrome differed with age. Only the children had widespread decreases in fractional anisotropy, mainly in mid- and long-range tracts, and they had more tracts with decreased fractional anisotropy than the adults. Only the adults had white matter volume loss, which was associated with decreased cortical surface area. The authors proposed that these findings define a TUBB3 E410K neuroimaging endophenotype. They hypothesized that the age-related changes result from microscopic misguided axons within each hemisphere that are pruned during maturation.
quotes: While only pediatric subjects had diffuse decreases in FA predominantly affecting mid- and long-range tracts, only adult subjects had white matter volume loss associated with decreased cortical surface area.
Furthermore, pediatric subjects had more tracts with decreased FA compared with controls than did adult subjects.

These findings define a TUBB3 E410K neuroimaging endophenotype and lead to the hypothesis that the age-related changes are due to microscopic intrahemispheric misguided axons that are pruned during maturation.

phenotypes.text: diffuse decreased white matter fractional anisotropy

relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome (CFEOM3A with anosmia and developmental delay) carrying the c.1228G>A (p.E410K) mutation, adding osteoporosis and cough syncope to the phenotype.

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2018) reported a 31-year-old Japanese woman who had been diagnosed with atypical Moebius syndrome because of congenital facial weakness and extraocular ophthalmoplegia sparing abduction. At age 23 years she had a femoral neck fracture, and studies showed osteoporosis due to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. She also had borderline intellectual disability, cyclic vomiting, syncope with cough, and decreased sense of smell since childhood. Brain MRI showed abnormal morphology of the corpus callosum and pons, with hypoplastic bilateral oculomotor and facial nerves.
quotes: The patient is a 31-year-old Japanese woman who was diagnosed with atypical Moebius syndrome because of congenital facial weakness and extraocular ophthalmoplegia sparing abduction.
She suffered a femoral neck fracture at 23 years of age, and radiological and endocrinological studies revealed osteoporosis because of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

She also had borderline intellectual disability, cyclic vomiting, syncope with cough, and decreased sense of smell since childhood. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed abnormal morphology of the corpus callosum and pontine. Hypoplastic bilateral oculomotor and facial nerves were evident.

findings.statement: In a 31-year-old Japanese woman with features of the TUBB3 E410K syndrome, previously diagnosed as atypical Moebius syndrome, Nakamura et al. (2018) identified a heterozygous c.1228G>A (p.E410K) mutation in the TUBB3 gene by targeted analysis of TUBB3.
quotes: we analyzed the TUBB3 gene and identified a heterozygous c.1228G > A (p.E410K) mutation that confirmed the diagnosis of TUBB3 E410K syndrome.

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2018) concluded that TUBB3 E410K syndrome may be misdiagnosed as atypical Moebius syndrome because of overlapping clinical features, and that genetic analysis for c.1228G>A in TUBB3 is useful to distinguish it from other disorders with congenital external ophthalmoplegia and facial nerve palsy.
quotes: TUBB3 E410K syndrome may be diagnosed as atypical Moebius syndrome because of overlapping clinical symptoms.
Genetic analysis of c.1228G > A in TUBB3 is useful to differentiate TUBB3 E410K syndrome from other disorders presenting congenital external ophthalmoplegia and facial nerve palsy.

relevance_reason: Reports the first familial (autosomal dominant) transmission of TUBB3 E410K syndrome, the disorder defining this entry, with clinical and endocrine phenotype variability.

findings.statement: Balasubramanian et al. (2015) described a female proband with TUBB3 E410K syndrome who had congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles (CFEOM), facial weakness, intellectual and social disabilities, and anosmia, but who had normal sexual development at puberty and three spontaneous pregnancies. Her 3 affected sons had nonendocrine features similar to their mother but, in addition, had variable features suggestive of additional endocrine abnormalities.
quotes: A de novo TUBB3 c.1228G>A mutation arose in a female proband who displayed CFEOM, facial weakness, intellectual and social disabilities, and anosmia. However, she underwent normal sexual development at puberty and had three spontaneous pregnancies
All sons displayed nonendocrine features of the TUBB3 E410K syndrome similar to their mother but, in addition, had variable features suggestive of additional endocrine abnormalities.

phenotypes.text: congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in mother (normal puberty and fertility)

findings.statement: Balasubramanian et al. (2015) found that the female proband carried a de novo heterozygous c.1228G>A (E410K) mutation in TUBB3, which was transmitted to all 3 of her affected sons, representing the first report of autosomal dominant inheritance of this mutation; all previously reported E410K subjects had been sporadic.
quotes: A de novo TUBB3 c.1228G>A mutation arose in a female proband
had three spontaneous pregnancies with subsequent autosomal-dominant inheritance of the mutation by her three boys
This first report of an autosomal-dominant inheritance of the TUBB3 c.1228G>A mutation in a family

findings.statement: Balasubramanian et al. (2015) reported autosomal dominant transmission of the TUBB3 E410K mutation from an affected mother to her 3 sons, noting that this complicates genetic counseling for families with the syndrome.
quotes: This first report of an autosomal-dominant inheritance of the TUBB3 c.1228G>A mutation in a family provides new insights into the spectrum and variability of endocrine phenotypes
These observations emphasize the need for appropriate clinical evaluation and complicate genetic counseling of patients and families with this syndrome.

relevance_reason: Defines the TUBB3 E410K syndrome (CFEOM3 with anosmia/Kallmann features and developmental delay) in 8 unrelated individuals with de novo c.1228G>A.

findings.statement: Chew et al. (2013) reported detailed phenotypes of 8 unrelated individuals with the TUBB3 E410K substitution, defining the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome': congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles, facial weakness, developmental delay and intellectual disabilities, and a progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy confirmed by electrophysiology. The phenotype was expanded to include Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia), stereotyped midface hypoplasia, and in some cases vocal cord paralysis, tracheomalacia and cyclic vomiting.
quotes: We report the detailed phenotypes of eight unrelated individuals who harbour this de novo mutation, and thus define the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome'.

We now confirm by electrophysiology that a progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy does indeed segregate with the mutation, and expand the TUBB3 E410K phenotype to include Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia), stereotyped midface hypoplasia, intellectual disabilities and, in some cases, vocal cord paralysis, tracheomalacia and cyclic vomiting.
Individuals harbouring this mutation were previously reported to have congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles, facial weakness, developmental delay and possible peripheral neuropathy.

phenotypes.text: congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles

findings.statement: Chew et al. (2013) found on neuroimaging of individuals with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome a thin corpus callosum and anterior commissure, and hypoplastic to absent olfactory sulci, olfactory bulbs, and oculomotor and facial nerves, supporting underlying abnormalities in axon guidance and maintenance.
quotes: Neuroimaging reveals a thin corpus callosum and anterior commissure, and hypoplastic to absent olfactory sulci, olfactory bulbs and oculomotor and facial nerves, which support underlying abnormalities in axon guidance and maintenance.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal morphology of the olfactory bulb

findings.statement: Chew et al. (2013) found the de novo heterozygous c.1228G>A mutation in TUBB3, resulting in a glu410-to-lys (E410K) substitution that directly alters a kinesin motor protein binding site, in 8 unrelated individuals with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome. The authors concluded that E410K defines a new genetic etiology for Moebius syndrome, Kallmann syndrome and cyclic vomiting.
quotes: c.1228G>A results in a TUBB3 E410K amino acid substitution that directly alters a kinesin motor protein binding site.
We report the detailed phenotypes of eight unrelated individuals who harbour this de novo mutation
Thus, the E410K substitution defines a new genetic aetiology for Moebius syndrome, Kallmann syndrome and cyclic vomiting.

findings.statement: Chew et al. (2013) found that the c.1228G>A mutation was absent in DNA from approximately 600 individuals with Kallmann syndrome or isolated or syndromic ocular and/or facial dysmotility disorders who lacked the combined features of the TUBB3 E410K syndrome, highlighting the specificity of the phenotype-genotype correlation and allowing prediction of the mutation from clinical features alone.
quotes: the c.1228G>A mutation was absent in DNA from ∼600 individuals who had either Kallmann syndrome or isolated or syndromic ocular and/or facial dysmotility disorders, but who did not have the combined features of the TUBB3 E410K syndrome, highlighting the specificity of this phenotype-genotype correlation.

relevance_reason: This paper first reports the heterozygous TUBB3 missense mutations behind CFEOM3 with extra neurological features ("TUBB3 syndromes"). These include E410K, R262H, D417H and R380C, which cause CFEOM3 with developmental delay, facial weakness and brain malformations. The paper also gives genotype-phenotype correlations, a knock-in mouse model, and in vitro and yeast functional studies. Anosmia is not mentioned.

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified 8 different heterozygous missense mutations in TUBB3, altering 6 amino acid residues, in 29 unrelated families with CFEOM3. CFEOM3 occurred either alone or as part of neurological syndromes that the authors called the TUBB3 syndromes. Each mutation segregated with the phenotype, was absent in the parents of sporadic patients, and was not found on more than 1,700 control chromosomes.
quotes: In 29 unrelated families, we identified eight unique heterozygous missense mutations that alter six amino acid residues.
Each of the eight mutations segregated with the TUBB3 phenotype, was absent in parents of sporadic individuals, and was not present on over 1700 control chromosomes.

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) sequenced TUBB3 in probands with CFEOM plus additional neurological symptoms. They identified a heterozygous 1228G>A transition, causing a glu410-to-lys (E410K) substitution, in 6 pedigrees. In each case the mutation arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germline mosaicism.
quotes: The remaining mutations, 1138C>T (R380C), 785G>A (R262H), and 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) reported that all patients with the E410K substitution had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness. These patients also had more severe corpus callosum dysgenesis with mild to moderate intellectual, social and behavioral impairment. The oldest E410K patient developed lower-extremity weakness and sensory loss in the second to third decade, without congenital contractures.
quotes: whereas all participants with R262H, E410K, and D417H had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness
Individuals with A302T, E410K, R262H, and R380C had more severe CC dysgenesis and mild to moderate intellectual, social, and behavioral impairments.
Most subjects harboring D417N and the oldest patient harboring E410K developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in the second to third decade, all in the absence of congenital contractures

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous de novo 785G>A transition in TUBB3, causing an arg262-to-his (R262H) substitution, in 2 pedigrees. Patients had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness. They also had congenital wrist and finger contractures, including ulnar deviation of the hand, and developed lower-extremity weakness and sensory loss in the first decade.
quotes: The remaining mutations, 1138C>T (R380C), 785G>A (R262H), and 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism

All subjects harboring D417H or R262H were born with congenital wrist and finger contractures, suggesting maldevelopment of spinal motor neurons (Figure 1I), and developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in the first decade of life.
R262H also results in congenital ulnar deviation of the hand with joint contractures of the thumbs and fingers

phenotypes.text: lower extremity weakness and sensory loss

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous 1249G>C transversion in TUBB3, causing an asp417-to-his (D417H) substitution, which co-segregated in a dominant fashion in 1 pedigree. Affected members had severe CFEOM3, congenital facial weakness, congenital wrist and finger contractures, and early-onset lower-extremity weakness and sensory loss.
quotes: 1249G>C (D417H) and 1249G>A (D417N) alter the same residue and co-segregate in a dominant fashion in one and four pedigrees, respectively.

All subjects harboring D417H or R262H were born with congenital wrist and finger contractures, suggesting maldevelopment of spinal motor neurons (Figure 1I), and developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in the first decade of life.

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous 1138C>T transition in TUBB3, causing an arg380-to-cys (R380C) substitution, in 1 pedigree; it arose de novo or from presumed germline mosaicism. The 2 affected sibs had moderate to severe CFEOM3, agenesis of the corpus callosum and anterior commissure, dysmorphic basal ganglia, hypoplasia of the brainstem and mild vermian hypoplasia, and developmental delay.
quotes: The remaining mutations, 1138C>T (R380C), 785G>A (R262H), and 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism
(G) Both R380C siblings have CC agenesis, and brainstem (arrow) and mild vermian hypoplasia (asterisk).
CFEOM3 with developmental delay, CC agenesis, and basal ganglia dysmorphisms in the absence of facial weakness may be predictive of the R380C substitution.

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous 1249G>A transition in TUBB3, causing an asp417-to-asn (D417N) substitution, which co-segregated dominantly in 4 pedigrees. Most carriers developed lower-extremity weakness and sensory loss in the second to third decade. Some carriers without CFEOM3 developed polyneuropathy, suggesting that TUBB3 mutations can cause an isolated CMT2-like disorder.
quotes: 1249G>C (D417H) and 1249G>A (D417N) alter the same residue and co-segregate in a dominant fashion in one and four pedigrees, respectively.
Several participants harboring D417N without CFEOM3 developed polyneuropathy (Table S1E), suggesting that TUBB3 mutations can cause an isolated CMT2-like disorder.

findings.statement: In families with isolated CFEOM3, including the 16q-linked pedigrees BN and DP, Tischfield et al. (2010) identified 3 heterozygous TUBB3 missense changes in 15 unrelated pedigrees: 784C>T (R262C) in 11, 904G>A (A302T) in 3, and 185G>A (R62Q) in 1.
quotes: We identified three heterozygous TUBB3 missense changes in 15 unrelated pedigrees: 784C>T (R262C) in 11 pedigrees, 904G>A (A302T) in three pedigrees, and 185G>A (R62Q) in one pedigree

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) reviewed brain MRI from patients with each TUBB3 mutation except D417H; imaging was normal only in the R62Q patient. Common findings were dysgenesis of the corpus callosum, anterior commissure and internal capsule, generalized loss of white matter, and basal ganglia dysmorphisms. No patient had cortical dysplasia or evidence of cortical migration defects. The severity of intellectual and behavioral impairment generally correlated with the severity of corpus callosum dysgenesis.
quotes: Common findings were dysgenesis of the corpus callosum (CC), anterior commissure (AC), and internal capsule; generalized loss of white matter; and basal ganglia dysmorphisms that correlated with specific mutations (Figure 2). No images showed cortical dysplasia or evidence of cortical migration defects.
Intellectual and behavioral impairments generally correlated with the severity of CC dysgenesis.

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) reported that many patients had aberrant eye movements and Marcus Gunn jaw-winking synkinesis. Orbital MRI in R262C and D417N pedigrees showed hypoplasia of the oculomotor nerve and of the levator palpebrae superioris, superior rectus and medial rectus muscles, with aberrant innervation of the lateral rectus by the oculomotor nerve. Electromyography showed a chronic, predominantly axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, diagnosed as CMT2 in some patients.
quotes: we found hypoplasia of the oculomotor nerve and the muscles innervated by its superior division - the levator palpebrae superioris and superior rectus - as well as the medial rectus muscle innervated by its inferior division
Electromyography revealed chronic, generalized sensorimotor polyneuropathy that was predominantly axonal, and diagnosed as Charcot-Marie-Tooth Type 2 (CMT2) in some subjects.

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that phenotypes limited to CFEOM3 and polyneuropathy often segregated in autosomal dominant families, whereas more severe phenotypes typically arose de novo. Severe CFEOM3 with facial weakness, developmental delay, moderate to severe corpus callosum dysgenesis and probably late-onset polyneuropathy predicted E410K. The additional presence of finger contractures, basal ganglia dysmorphisms and early-onset polyneuropathy suggested R262H or D417H.
quotes: while the TUBB3 phenotypes limited to CFEOM3 and polyneuropathy often segregate in autosomal dominant families, those with more severe clinical findings typically arise de novo.

Association of severe CFEOM3 with facial weakness, developmental delay, moderate to severe CC dysgenesis and likely a late-onset polyneuropathy predicts the E410K substitution, while the addition of finger contractures, basal ganglia dysmorphisms, and early onset polyneuropathy would suggest R262H or D417H substitutions.

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) generated knock-in mice carrying the R262C substitution in Tubb3. Heterozygous mice appeared healthy, whereas homozygotes died within hours of birth. Homozygotes had normal cortical layering but showed anterior commissure defects, corpus callosum agenesis with Probst bundles in 2 of 5, and misguidance of the oculomotor, trochlear and trigeminal nerves. They also had reduced Tubb3 protein, increased microtubule stability, and reduced Kif21a binding to microtubules.
quotes: By contrast, Tubb3R262C/R262C mice failed to breathe normally and died within hours of birth.
Agenesis of the CC with bundles of stalled axons (Probst bundles) adjacent to the midline was observed in 2/5 homozygous mutant mice
A significant decrease of Kif21a was detected with microtubules from the brains of Tubb3R262C/R262C mice (Figure 4E).

findings.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) expressed the mutants in reticulocyte lysate. R62Q, R262C, A302T and R380C markedly reduced heterodimer formation, whereas R262H, E410K and D417H/N formed heterodimers that cycled like wildtype. When the 8 substitutions were modeled in yeast, all altered microtubule dynamics and conferred benomyl resistance. R262C/H, E410K and D417H/N reduced plus-end accumulation of the kinesins Kip3p and Kip2p. The authors suggested that the mutations act through dominant effects on microtubule function, and that facial paralysis and polyneuropathy occur only with the 4 mutations that allow heterodimer formation and disrupt kinesin interactions.
quotes: Under native conditions, R62Q, R262C, A302T, and R380C showed significant reductions in heterodimer yield, whereas the remaining four mutants generated moderate yields (Figure 4F).
Thus, the R262C, R262H, E410K, D417N, and D417H substitutions result in a significant decrease in Kip3p-3YFP and Kip2p-3YFP accumulation on microtubule plus-ends

Second, facial paralysis and progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy occur only in those individuals harboring R262H, E410K, D417H/N, the four mutations that permit heterodimer formation and efficient microtubule incorporation, and have dominant effects upon microtubule function by perturbing kinesin interactions in yeast.
